72985-the-tower.title: The Tower
72985-the-tower.creator: W. B. Yeats
72985-the-tower.description: A book by W. B. Yeats. Once out of nature I shall never take   My bodily form from any natural thing,   But such a form as Grecian goldsmiths make   Of hammered gold and gold enamelling   To keep a drowsy emperor awake;   Or set upon a golden bough to sing   To lords and ladies of Byzantium   Of what is past, or passing, or to come.

arxiv-2102-06446.title: Fully-connected bond percolation on ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d}
arxiv-2102-06446.creator: David Dereudre
arxiv-2102-06446.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by David Dereudre. We consider the bond percolation model on the lattice ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} ( d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 ) with the constraint to be fully connected. Each edge is open with probability p ∈ ( 0 , 1 ) p\in(0,1) , closed with probability 1 − p 1-p and then the process is conditioned to have a unique open connected component (bounded or unbounded).

arxiv-2106-12955.title: Regularisation for PCA- and SVD-type matrix factorisations Journal: Ambient Intelligence and Humanized Computing
arxiv-2106-12955.creator: Abdolrahman Khoshrou, Eric J. Pauwels
arxiv-2106-12955.description: Abstract Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and its close relative, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), are well-known linear matrix decomposition techniques that are widely used in applications such as dimension reduction and clustering. However, an important limitation of SVD/PCA is its sensitivity to noise in the input data.

arxiv-2202-12695.title: Measuring Shocks to Central Bank Independence using Legal Rulings Thanks: The authors are grateful to Marek Jarociński for providing many helpful suggestions and parts of the dataset. Huber and Pfarrhofer gratefully acknowledge financial support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF, grant no. ZK 35)
arxiv-2202-12695.creator: Stefan Griller, Florian Huber, Michael Pfarrhofer
arxiv-2202-12695.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Stefan Griller, Florian Huber, Michael Pfarrhofer. We investigate the consequences of legal rulings on the conduct of monetary policy. Several unconventional monetary policy measures of the European Central Bank have come under scrutiny before national courts and the European Court of Justice. These lawsuits have the potential to severely impact the scope and flexibility of central bank policies, and central bank independence in a wide sense, with important consequences for the real and financial economy.

arxiv-2308-15194.title: Ensemble of Counterfactual Explainers
arxiv-2308-15194.creator: Riccardo Guidotti ✉, Salvatore Ruggieri
arxiv-2308-15194.description: Abstract In eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), several counterfactual explainers have been proposed, each focusing on some desirable properties of counterfactual instances: minimality, actionability, stability, diversity, plausibility, discriminative power. We propose an ensemble of counterfactual explainers that boosts weak explainers, which provide only a subset of such properties, to a powerful method covering all of them.

arxiv-2309-16099.title: Nonparametric estimation of a covariate-adjusted counterfactual treatment regimen response curve
arxiv-2309-16099.creator: Ashkan Ertefaie, Luke Duttweiler, Brent A. Johnson, Mark J. van der Laan
arxiv-2309-16099.description: Abstract Flexible estimation of the mean outcome under a treatment regimen (i.e., value function) is the key step toward personalized medicine. We define our target parameter as a conditional value function given a set of baseline covariates which we refer to as a stratum based value function.

arxiv-2312-15890.title: Towards Robust Multimodal Prompting with Missing Modalities
arxiv-2312-15890.creator: Jaehyuk Jang, Yooseung Wang, Changick Kim
arxiv-2312-15890.description: Abstract Recently, multimodal prompting, which introduces learnable missing-aware prompts for all missing modality cases, has exhibited impressive performance. However, it encounters two critical issues: 1) The number of prompts grows exponentially as the number of modalities increases; and 2) It lacks robustness in scenarios with different missing modality settings between training and inference.

arxiv-2403-16890.title: A low-order locking-free multiscale finite element method for isotropic elasticity Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
arxiv-2403-16890.creator: Antônio Tadeu A. Gomes, Weslley S. Pereira, Frédéric Valentin
arxiv-2403-16890.description: Abstract The multiscale hybrid-mixed (MHM) method consists of a multi-level strategy to approximate the solution of boundary value problems with heterogeneous coefficients. In this context, we propose a family of low-order finite elements for the linear elasticity problem which are free from Poisson locking.

arxiv-2503-23110.title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of edges
arxiv-2503-23110.creator: Katarzyna Rybarczyk, Grzegorz Serafin
arxiv-2503-23110.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Katarzyna Rybarczyk, Grzegorz Serafin. We investigate the subgraph count in the random intersection graph model 𝒢 ⁡ ( n ​ ; ​ m ​ ; ​ p ) \mathcal{G}(n\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}m\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}p) . Due to substantial edge dependencies, studying even such fundamental statistics is significantly more challenging than in the classical binomial model 𝒢 ⁡ ( n ​ ; ​ p ) \mathcal{G}(n\mathord{\mathchar 59\relax}p) . This article establish new normal approximation bounds in both the Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances for general non-degenerate U U -statistics.

arxiv-2512-18819.title: Locational Marginal Emissions for Carbon-Aware Data Center Operations in Large-Scale Power Grids
arxiv-2512-18819.creator: Luc Cote, Andy Sun
arxiv-2512-18819.description: Abstract SUMMARY Carbon accounting methods for electricity consumption face challenges regarding physical deliverability, double counting, additionality, and impact magnitude. Locational Marginal Emissions (LMEs) show potential to address many of these key issues. However, their use in a large-scale power grids remains understudied.

pmc-11381857.title: Research paper: Two cases of multiple osteoid osteomas in young patients treated with cryoablation: Diagnosis, technical efficacy, and follow-up
pmc-11381857.creator: Antonios Michailidis, Ilia Anastasiadi, Panagiotis Kosmoliaptsis, G George Dimou, Sophia Zlika, Christos Giankoulof, Ioannis Tsifountoudis, Stavros Galanis, Evangelos Petsatodis
pmc-11381857.description: Osteoid osteomas are benign bone tumors characterized by severe localized pain, often challenging the daily lives of young patients. While these tumors are typically solitary, rare cases of multiple osteoid osteomas have been reported. This research paper presents a case series of 2 young patients with multiple osteoid osteomas, highlighting their clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, treatment with cryoablation, and follow-up.

pmc-12526433.title: Coefficient of Thermal Expansion of AlSi10Mg, 316L Stainless Steel and Ti6Al4V Alloys Made with Laser Powder Bed Fusion
pmc-12526433.creator: Selami Emanet, Edem Honu, Kekeli Agbewornu, Evelyn Quansah, Congyuan Zeng, Patrick Mensah
pmc-12526433.description: This study investigates the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) behavior of LPBF-fabricated AlSi10Mg, 316L stainless steel, and Ti-6Al-4V alloys, focusing on the influence of laser power, scanning speed, and annealing. AlSi10Mg exhibits the highest CTE, but its thermal expansion is highly sensitive to porosity and balling defects.

pmc-12676176.title: Closing GDMT Gaps in PAD Patients During Supervised Exercise Therapy
pmc-12676176.creator: S.M. Muir, A.R. Albers
pmc-12676176.description: BackgroundPeripheral artery disease carries high cardiovascular risk. Although supervised exercise therapy (SET) improves function, uptake of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is inconsistent in practice.Project RationaleWe observed frequent missed opportunities for GDMT among patients with peripheral artery disease who were referred to a high-touch SET program.

pmc-12785425.title: Dynamic Behavioral and Molecular Changes Induced by Chronic Restraint Stress Exposure in Mice
pmc-12785425.creator: Thomas D. Prevot, Jaime K. Knoch, Dipashree Chatterjee, Sierra Codeluppi-Arrowsmith, Keith A. Misquitta, Corey J. E. Fee, Dwight Newton, Hyunjung Oh, Etienne Sibille, Mounira Banasr
pmc-12785425.description: Chronic stress is a major risk factor contributing to cellular changes in the brain that precipitate the emergence of various behavioral changes, including anxiety and anhedonia—symptoms relevant to mood disorders including major depression—however the sequence and trajectory of early molecular changes is poorly characterized.

pmc-13227351.title: Ticagrelor Versus Clopidogrel in Patients With ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Elevated Platelet Counts: A Multicenter Comparative Analysis of Ischemic Outcomes
pmc-13227351.creator: Fang-Jie Ji, Xian Shao, Tian-Shu Gu, Yu-Kun Zhang, Su-Tao Hu, Chao Jiang, Jing-Kun Zhang, Xue Wu, Seung-Woon Rha, Xing Liu, Tong Liu, Kang-Yin Chen
pmc-13227351.description: Background:Dual antiplatelet therapy is essential for managing ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI); however, the optimal choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in patients with thrombocytosis remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the effects of clopidogrel and ticagrelor on the prognosis of patients with STEMI and platelet counts exceeding 350 × 109/L.

pmc-13386847.title: Current evidence does not demonstrate decreased ICU length of stay and delirium incidence associated with the use of volatile sedation in critically ill patients: re-analysis of data from a recent systematic review
pmc-13386847.creator: Jiawen Deng
pmc-13386847.description: lled trials, the reviewers reported that volatile sedation significantly decreased awakening time, time to extubation, ICU length of stay, and incidence of delirium. Unfortunately, these conclusions rest on improper application of systematic review methodologies, inclusion of multiple ineligible studies, and major errors in the extracted data.

pmc-13394787.title: Evaluating species identification apps as a tool for small plot-based surveys of vascular plants in Alberta, Canada
pmc-13394787.creator: Iyesha M Wanigasinghe, Diane L Haughland, Lysandra A Pyle, Mary A L Villeneuve, Scott E Nielsen
pmc-13394787.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). While mobile apps are becoming more accurate at identifying vascular plants, it is unclear whether accuracy is maintained when doing plot-based surveys, where image acquisition is limited to a small pool of individuals that often lack ideal identification features. We evaluated two free plant identification apps, Flora Incognita and iNaturalist, using 5291 field images of 119 species from 54 plots of 0.8 m2, from graminoid-dominated grassland and forested sites.
